content.text: During delivery, the turtle sign may occur (retraction of the baby’s head, similar to a turtle retracting into its shell) or a red, puffy face
brachial plexus injuries d/t traction during shoulder dystocia, Erb’s palsy, Klumpke paralysis, Cerebral palsy

Erb-Duchenne palsy: a lesion in the upper trunk (root) injury (C5-C6 +/- C7) of the brachial plexus, leading to the characteristic “waiter’s tip” deformity (arm in adduction w/ elbow extension, forearm pronation, & wrist flexion w/ fingers curled up)
McRobert’s Maneuver: hyperflexion & abduction of the mother’s hips towards the abdomen w/ application of suprapubic pressure
Wood screw maneuver: anterior should pushed towards chest, posterior shoulder pushed towards back
Zavanelli Maneuver: fetal head is flexed & pushed back into the vaginal canal followed immediately by delivery via c-section (LAST RESORT)
